title: Quant switchover error-envelope scan (APR 2024)
content:
Purpose and short story:
This is an exploratory sweep to identify practical switchover boundaries (the "error envelope") where we should route live requests from high-throughput low-precision kernels to higher-fidelity kernels or model variants. Goal: codify simple rules that recover most quality while preserving cost/latency wins from INT8/AWQ/FP8 runs.

Scope and motivations:
- Not a full QA; focused on interactive generation workloads (1-2 turn chat, typical token lengths 32-256).
- We want a tiny decision surface: when p95 latency is within SLO but expected quality regret (relative to FP16 baseline) exceeds threshold X, then switchover.
- Compare quant methods: per-channel INT8 (symmetric), block-AWQ, GPTQ (per-layer quant), and FP8 (E4M3-like simulated).
- Kernel variants: vectorized-matmul (low-latency), tiled-gemm (stable for AWQ), fallback-ref (baseline).

Experimental setup:
- Model: opensource LLM-13B-like checkpoint (decoder-only), trimmed to production-compatible tokenizer.
- Host: single A100-80GB equivalent for kernel-local tests; separate small cluster for multi-kernel interference tests.
- Client workload: 10k requests sampled from production prompt corpus (search snippets, support transcripts), request length distribution: p25=20, p50=48, p75=96, p90=180, p99=400 tokens.
- Metrics collected per request: latency_ms (total), tokens_generated, model_variant, kernel, quant_method, BLEU-like similarity to FP16 baseline, perplexity_ratio, topk-agreement (k=5), cost_estimate_usd_per_1k_requests.
- Quality regressions represented as "regret" = 1 - topk-agreement (FP16 top-1 baseline). We also compute LMDelta = (crossentropy_quant - crossentropy_fp16)/crossentropy_fp16.

Sweep design:
- For each quant_method x kernel combination run batch of 10k requests single-threaded client to measure clean latencies and quality.
- For each combination, sweep request concurrency from 1 -> 32 to see how switchover boundaries shift under queuing.
- Produce a 2D surface: latency_ratio (quant/kernel) vs median_regret. We will mark iso-regret contours (0.5%, 1%, 2.5%, 5%).

Representative results (summary):
- INT8 (per-channel, symmetric) on vectorized-matmul: p50 latency = 18ms, p95 = 62ms, median_regret = 0.9% (but tail has rare spikes up to 8% for long prompts where activation clipping happened).
- AWQ block-quant on tiled-gemm: p50 = 24ms, p95 = 70ms, median_regret = 1.8%, 95th-errile (95% quantile of regret) = 3.6%. More stable for long contexts.
- GPTQ (per-layer) on fallback-ref kernel: p50 = 48ms, p95 = 120ms, median_regret = 0.4% (best quality but ~2x latency).
- FP8 emulated on vectorized-matmul: p50 = 22ms, p95 = 68ms, median_regret = 0.6%, but shows increased variance under mixed-workload interference.

Key observations:
1) Error envelope is non-linear with latency. At low latencies (p95 < 70ms) median_regret moves quickly from ~0.5% to ~2.5% with small kernel/quant changes.
2) Long-context prompts amplify INT8 instability: activation saturation/clipping causes outlier tokens with extremely high regret; this shows up as heavy right tail in regret distribution.
3) AWQ shows better tail-behavior for long contexts but slightly worse median. GPTQ holds quality across lengths but costs ~2x-3x in latency and 1.8x cost.
4) Under concurrency (>=8), vectorized kernels saturate and start showing queueing latency that shifts switchover boundary — i.e., you might prefer a slightly slower but more stable kernel under multi-tenant load.

Proposed switchover candidate rule sets (simple heuristics):
- Static threshold rule A (latency-first): If p95_latency_estimate < 80ms AND expected_median_regret < 1% => use INT8 vectorized; else if median_regret in [1%, 3%] => AWQ tiled; else GPTQ fallback.
- Tail-aware rule B (tail-first): If expected_95th_regret > 3% OR prompt_length_estimate > 256 => route to AWQ or GPTQ immediately.
- Cost-sensitivity rule C: allow INT8 for <= 1k tokens/customer-month; otherwise prefer AWQ for balance. (placeholder for billing hooks)

Micro-profiling notes (commands and traces):
- Collected nvprof-like traces; kernel time breakdown shows matmul op time dominates as expected, but quant/dequant overheads are non-trivial when using per-token casting on vectorized path (adds ~2.5ms per 128 tokens).
- KV cache touch patterns: INT8 reduced memory pressure but caused more frequent L2->L1 fetches on tiled kernels causing jitter.

Failure / edge cases observed:
- Activation clip mode: certain prompts with many rare tokens cause activation ranges to exceed calibration quantization ranges (seen in INT8 runs). Need better per-request fallback or range-adaptive quant clamps.
- Off-by-one token divergence: small rounding differences cascade after ~80 tokens on some AWQ runs leading to different completions that increase measured regret (not necessarily a human-noticeable difference).

Actionable next steps (short list):
1) Implement cheap switchover estimator in runtime: use a 1-5 token micro-eval on prefix to predict 95th-regret probability; cheap sampling approach. (Assigned: Ben)
2) Add simple range-adaptive clamp mode for INT8 paths to reduce activation clip spikes; build guard that falls back to AWQ on detection. (Assigned: Diego)
3) Run multi-tenant interference sweep with AWQ vectorized kernels in a 3-node cluster to measure stability at production load curves. (Assigned: Mei)
4) Bake in policy A (latency-first) as a default in canary for 2 weeks, collect metrics, and measure customer-visible regressions with small eval-set. (Assigned: Aisha)

Open questions / discussion points:
- How to set regret thresholds in a way that maps to human-perceived quality (not only topk agreement)? Need human eval subset or quality heuristics.
- Pricing signals: can we expose dynamic-cost-awareness to customers (e.g., cheaply prefer INT8 but with an SLA for quality)?
- Is it feasible to do fast on-request micro-evals without doubling median latency? Early testing suggests sub-5ms if we reuse warmed kernels.

Appendix (quick tables):
- Example single-run summary (vectorized INT8): p50=18ms, p95=62ms, median_regret=0.009, 95th_regret=0.08, cost_est=0.28$ per 1k
- AWQ tiled example: p50=24ms, p95=70ms, median_regret=0.018, 95th_regret=0.036, cost_est=0.36$ per 1k
- GPTQ fallback: p50=48ms, p95=120ms, median_regret=0.004, 95th_regret=0.009, cost_est=0.62$ per 1k

Notes to reviewers:
- This is exploratory; numbers depend heavily on model shape and tokenization. Please look at the linked PR with raw CSVs (PR#3984) for full distributions.
- We should standardize a small eval set (50 prompts per workload type) to map regret->human delta.

Quick todo: attach raw traces, lite script to reproduce sample workloads, and a short runbook for the canary policy.

-- Aisha
